words.gloss: those things which are not real

ai.literal: Reality not-being-those-things as reality thus perceiving by-delusion arises ignoble birth.
ai.translation: From the delusion that perceives things which are not real as real, arises the ignoble cycle of birth.
ai.modern: மெய்ப்பொருள் அல்லாதவற்றை மெய்ப்பொருள் என்று தவறாக உணர்கின்ற அறியாமையினால், சிறப்பற்ற பிறவித் துன்பம் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the root cause of the cycle of rebirth and suffering. The key word 'maruḷ' (delusion) refers to the mental darkness that mistakes transient, unreal things ('poruḷ allavaṟṟai') for the eternal, ultimate truth ('poruḷ'). When a person perceives the illusory world as the ultimate reality, they develop attachments. This delusion leads to 'māṇā piṟappu' (ignoble or worthless birth), which represents the continuous cycle of rebirths filled with suffering.

ai.literal: Darkness having departed, happiness will yield, to those of blemish-free vision, delusion having departed.
ai.translation: For those who possess a flawless vision free from delusion, the darkness of ignorance will depart, yielding true happiness.
ai.modern: மயக்கம் நீங்கி, குற்றமற்ற மெய்யறிவு பெற்றவர்க்கு, அறியாமை என்னும் இருள் விலகி, அது பேரின்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the transformative power of true perception. For those who have freed themselves from delusion (மருள்) and attained a flawless, blemish-free vision (மாசறு காட்சி) of reality, the darkness of ignorance (இருள்) is completely removed. In its place, they experience a lasting and profound happiness (இன்பம்). The poet contrasts the darkness of delusion with the light of pure vision, showing that spiritual clarity naturally leads to ultimate bliss.

words.gloss: to those who have attained clarity

ai.literal: From doubt having freed themselves, to those who have attained clarity, than the earth, heaven nearer it has.
ai.translation: To those who have freed themselves from doubt and attained clear vision, heaven is closer than this earth.
ai.modern: ஐயத்திலிருந்து நீங்கி மெய்ப்பொருளைத் தெளிவாக உணர்ந்தவர்களுக்கு, இவ்வுலகத்தை விட வானுலகம் மிக அருகில் உள்ளதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the state of those who have attained true knowledge. When a person removes all doubts (ஐயம்) and achieves absolute clarity of mind (தெளிவு), the ultimate state of liberation (வானம்) is closer to them than this physical earth (வையம்) they inhabit. The poet uses the word 'நணியது' (nearer) to emphasize that liberation is not a distant, unreachable goal but an immediate reality for the enlightened mind.

ai.literal: Five perception even when attained, benefit is indeed not, truth perception to those who lack.
ai.translation: Even if they have mastered the perception of all five senses, there is absolutely no benefit for those who lack the perception of the ultimate truth.
ai.modern: ஐம்புலன்களின் அறிவை முழுமையாகப் பெற்றிருந்த போதிலும், மெய்யறிவு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு அதனால் எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts sensory perception with the realization of ultimate truth. 'ஐயுணர்வு' refers to the knowledge gained through the five physical senses. Even if a person achieves complete mastery over these senses, it is of no real benefit ('பயமின்றே') if they lack 'மெய்யுணர்வு', which is the direct perception of reality. True wisdom lies beyond mere sensory experience, in understanding the fundamental truth of existence.

words.gloss: of whatever nature it may be

ai.literal: Whatever thing, of whatever nature it may be, that thing's true essence to discern is wisdom.
ai.translation: To discern the true essence of any thing, whatever its apparent nature may be, is wisdom.
ai.modern: எந்த ஒரு பொருளும் எத்தகைய தன்மையைக் கொண்டதாக இருந்தாலும், அப்பொருளின் உண்மையான இயல்பைக் காண்பதே அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the ability to look beyond superficial appearances to find the ultimate truth. Things in the world present themselves in various forms and natures, which can often be deceptive or temporary. True knowledge does not stop at these outward characteristics but penetrates to the core reality of the object. The word 'meypporuḷ' (true essence) contrasts with 'ettanmaittu' (whatever nature), emphasizing the difference between transient qualities and permanent truth.

ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the ultimate goal of realizing the truth. Those who study and successfully perceive the true, unchanging reality (மெய்ப்பொருள்) while in this world (ஈண்டு) will reach a state or path (நெறி) from which they do not return (வாரா) to the cycle of birth and death. The repetition of 'ஈண்டு' contrasts the present earthly life of learning with the state of liberation from returning here. The term 'தலைப்படுவர்' signifies firmly reaching or securing this supreme path.

ai.translation: If the mind investigates deeply and realizes the ultimate reality, there is absolutely no need to think of rebirth again.

ai.explanation: This couplet explains the ultimate benefit of realizing the truth. When the mind investigates deeply and perceives the true nature of reality, it attains liberation. Consequently, there is absolutely no need to experience or contemplate rebirth ever again. The word 'உள்ளது' refers to the ultimate reality or truth, and 'ஓர்த்து' emphasizes the role of deep, critical inquiry in reaching this realization.

ai.literal: Birth-called ignorance to depart, liberation-called Ultimate Reality perceiving is wisdom.
ai.translation: True wisdom is to perceive the Ultimate Reality, which is called liberation, so that the ignorance called birth may depart.
ai.modern: பிறப்பு என்று சொல்லப்படும் அறியாமை நீங்குவதற்காக, வீடுபேறு என்று சொல்லப்படும் செம்பொருளைக் காண்பதே உண்மையான அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the direct perception of the Ultimate Reality (செம்பொருள்). The poet equates the cycle of birth (பிறப்பு) with ignorance (பேதைமை), suggesting that physical existence is a state of delusion. To remove this ignorance, one must perceive the supreme truth, which is identified with liberation or excellence (சிறப்பு). Therefore, true knowledge is not academic learning, but the spiritual insight that dissolves delusion and ends the cycle of rebirth.

ai.literal: Having understood the true support, if one conducts oneself so that worldly attachments perish, then the afflicting sufferings that usually attach will be destroyed and will not attach again.
ai.translation: If one realizes the true support of all and lives so that worldly attachments perish, the afflictions that normally cling to life will be destroyed and will never cling again.
ai.modern: உண்மையான பற்றை உணர்ந்து, உலகப் பற்றுகள் அழியுமாறு வாழ்ந்தால், தொடர்ந்து வந்து பற்றுகின்ற பிறவித்துன்பங்கள் அழிந்து மீண்டும் வந்து பற்ற மாட்டா.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the word 'சார்பு' in two different senses to guide the seeker. The first 'சார்பு' refers to the ultimate reality or true support of existence, which one must realize. The second 'சார்பு' refers to worldly attachments and dependencies that must be destroyed. When a person lives with this realization, the 'சார்தரு நோய்'—the recurring sufferings of birth and rebirth that naturally cling to human life—are completely destroyed and will never return.

ai.literal: Desire, anger, delusion, of these three, the name to perish, will perish suffering.
ai.translation: When the very names of these three—desire, anger, and delusion—are utterly destroyed, all suffering will also perish.
ai.modern: விருப்பம், சினம், அறியாமை ஆகிய இந்த மூன்றின் பெயரும் அழியும்படி ஒழிந்தால், பிறவித்துன்பம் அழியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the path to liberation by identifying the three root causes of all human suffering: desire (kāmam), anger (vekuḷi), and delusion or ignorance (mayakkam). The author asserts that suffering (nōy) is not merely reduced but completely eradicated when even the names or traces of these three defilements are wiped out. By using the word 'nāmam' (name), the verse emphasizes that the destruction of these vices must be so absolute that not even their memory or reputation remains in the mind. This complete purification leads to the cessation of all existential pain.
